A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ImplicitQA and contain readable main texts, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding experiments and supplementary material can be matched despite renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–F report original model evaluations, human performance, prompting experiments, and repeated-run statistics.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds evaluations of four models and a quantitative comparison of question diversity.

M1.justification: The FrameQuiz/ImplicitEval workflow, expert annotation and verification, categorization process, and structured GPT reasoning prompt are retained. No revised algorithm or proposed VideoQA architecture is documented.

E1.justification: V2 Table 2 newly analyzes question text from MVBench, TempCompass, Cinepile, and Movie-QA for diversity comparison. This extends the data used for analysis; the cinematic VideoQA domains and corresponding nine-category evaluations remain matched.

E2.justification: V2 Table 3 adds Gemma 3, InternVL 3, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude 4 Sonnet to the main 16-frame comparison. All earlier model families remain, substantially broadening both open-weight and proprietary comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 substantially revises the reported sample composition from 1K questions over 320+ clips to 1K questions over 1K clips, and introduces embedding-based cosine similarity for diversity evaluation. Existing frame and scale settings remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain whether clip-count units changed or experiments were rerun; human participation also becomes inconsistent between plural annotators in Section 4 and a singular annotator in Appendix F.

E4.justification: Section 3.1 adds an analysis testing question diversity against four datasets, and Appendix C.5 adds question word-count statistics alongside the existing character-length plot. Scaling, prompting, genre, media-type, difficulty, and qualitative analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Appendix E retains five independent Qwen2.5-VL runs and the same mean/standard-deviation reporting. V1 Table 5 and v2 Table 6 contain identical uncertainty values; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Four complete model-result rows are added, with overall accuracies of 42.1% for Gemma 3, 43.3% for InternVL 3, 49.6% for Gemini 2.5 Flash, and 45.4% for Claude 4 Sonnet. Earlier model scores remain unchanged. Human counting accuracy changes from 53.9% to 65.9% and macro accuracy from 84.3% to 85.6%, while overall accuracy remains 83.0%. New diversity results report ImplicitQA similarity of 0.161 versus 0.191–0.293 for the comparison datasets.

T1.justification: The existing hardness-score definition is retained. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The claimed dataset size changes from 320+ to 1K clips, and explicit causal-reasoning claims are narrowed toward motivational reasoning in the introduction, category description, and conclusion. The central benchmark contribution, novelty claim, and model–human performance gap remain.

C2.justification: V2 interprets lower question-embedding similarity as evidence of greater diversity and adds an Appendix F argument that human performance supports well-defined, solvable, validated questions. Existing explanations of scaling limitations and category difficulty are largely retained.

D1.justification: V1 provides dataset, annotation-tool, evaluation-tool, and evaluation-code links and states that resources are released. V2 removes these links and changes Appendix A to a planned release upon acceptance, materially reducing documented access and reproducibility. It newly identifies all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and Sentence Transformers for diversity analysis; GPU information is retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Table 1 add Open-EQA and VSI-Bench, contrasting their dense egocentric observations with ImplicitQA's implicit reasoning requirements. V2 also adds TimeLogic, diversity-measurement literature, and references for the four new models, while shortening several existing benchmark discussions.

P1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are rewritten, related-work descriptions are shortened, causal/motivational terminology is edited, and references move before the appendix. The main section sequence, appendix organization, and most explanatory prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adds a diversity table and word-count figure, expands the related-dataset and main model-comparison tables, and changes typography, figure sizing, and float placement. Most existing plots, qualitative panels, and interface illustrations are reused.

improvement.justification: Four additional model evaluations and quantitative diversity evidence strengthen the benchmark's empirical support. However, Appendix A removes concrete resource links and postpones release, while the unexplained clip-count revision and inconsistent human-annotator descriptions weaken reproducibility and clarity. These benefits and harms leave the net quality direction uncertain; the PDFs do not establish whether the revised dataset and human results reflect changed experiments or reporting corrections.
